Purpose of the Collective AAP Platform
The South Sudan Collective AAP Platform will strengthen how AAP data (what communities are telling us and asking us to act on) is systematically brought into strategic and operational decisionmaking.
The Platform will consolidate existing de-identified AAP data from a range of sources into a format that allows us to identify trends, identify emerging issues, and inform programmatic adjustments at the inter-agency level, and ensure that decisions from leadership are influenced by community data. title: المحافظة على الصلاة

text:
المحافظة على الصلاة
لا يؤذن الفجر إلا وقد أيقظ أولاده وبناته وأمهم..
فيقيم الصلاة وهو أمامهم..
ظل كل أفراد الأسرة على هذا النهج وتعود الأبناء جميعهم.. فأصبحوا يتنافسون فى القيام..
كبروا واستقل كل منهم ببيته.. يقضون ليلة الجمعة فى بيت العائلة الكبير مع أمهم وجدتهم وأبيهم وإحدى أخواتهم التى لم تتزوج.. يقضون تلك الليلة ولا ينصرفون إلا بعد صلاة الفجر..
انضم إليهم زوجاتهم وأزواج أخواتهم.. وبعد الصلاة يقرأون سورة الكهف ثم الدخان وبعدها الملك..
عائلة حافظت على صلواتها ووصالها..
توفى الأب ولحقته الأم..
فانقطع الوصل وأصبح كل منهم يصلى فى بيته آخذين ما تعودوا عليه..
رأى والده فى المنام وقد أخذ إخوانه وأخواته وتركه وحيدًا..
تكررت الرؤيا.. أصابه هم وغم.. وأخذ يذكر ويتذكر..
حتى رأى والد زوجته ومعه والدة زوجته وقد أقبلا عليه ليصلى بهما..
وعندما انتهت الصلاة استدار لأبى زوجته وأخذه جانباً وحكى له ما رأى وأنه أصابه غم.. ولم يعرف تأويل ذلك..
قال له.. هل ترك والدك وصية أو أمرك بأمر ولم تنفذه؟..
ثم كيف هى صلاتك؟..
فاعترف بأنه لا يصلى الصبح كما كان مع والده وأنه دائماً يصليه متأخراً..
قال له.. افعل لترى..

title: Living in bondage: Jimmy Odukoya and Lara Adeboye (1)
summary: A column on Jimmy Odukoya and the Fountain of Life Church leadership crisis, and the online backlash against Lara Adeboye over her relationship. Read More: https://punchng.com/living-in-bondage-jimmy-odukoya-and-lara-adeboye-1/
text:
For its bottomless depths, the human mind holds limitless possibilities. All at once, it is the most fertile soil and most barren wasteland ever, depending on its nurturing. Time and the mind are long-time friends, but one deceives the other oftentimes. In oscillatory motion, the hourglass dwindles in broad daylight; a while, and the glass is empty, and night falls. Time.
I have a mind, but no time. Don’t ask if my mind is barren or fertile; I know it could be both at once. Today, I need a fertile mind and scarce time. So, I unfurled my mind. “Roam, roam, roam free,” I said.
A hand grabbed me by the wrist and led me straight beside the still waters of the Osun Osogbo River. It was my mind. “Ògbéni,” why bring me to the grove, I asked. “Shhh! Keep quiet, watch and listen,” my mind ordered.
So, I watched the river flow quietly under the creaky Amítítí Bridge built in 1935 – a world-record monument in decay and dilapidation – with missing steps, guardrails and a gaping floor.

text:
الله يرحمك يا سادات
لو اختار حاذق أغنية تواكب تسليم الميدالية الذهبية لاسم السادات فى الكونجرس الأمريكى، لكانت كلمات طيب الذكر «بيرم التونسى» بألحان الموسيقار محمد الموجى، بصوت كوكب الشرق: «بالسلام إحنا بدينا... بالسلام / ردت الدنيا علينا... بالسلام / يا سلام... يا سلام... يا سلام... يا سلام».
وعزفت فرقة مشاة البحرية الأمريكية مقطعًا من أغنية «ليلة حب» من ألحان الموسيقار محمد عبد الوهاب، لتلون حفل الكونجرس بأجمل الألحان، كل ما يصدر عن عباقرة المحروسة يشدو به العالم، يطرب العالم لألحان المصريين وشدو بلابلهم منذ فجر البشرية الوردى.
لو كان كبير رسامى الكاريكاتير «مصطفى حسين» حيًّا، لأعاد نشر كاريكاتيره الشهير لفلاح كفر الهنادوة فخورًا بكلمات طيب الذكر كبير الساخرين «أحمد رجب»: «الله يرحمك يا سادات»، وأضيف من أقوال جدتى الطيبة: «ويبشبش الطوبة اللى تحت راسك» (ترحمًا).
لا يعرف الفضل لأهل الفضل إلا ذووه، وكلمة الرئيس السيسى فخورًا بتكريم السادات تحمل عظيم الامتنان لبطل الحرب والسلام، وعلى صفحته الرسمية على «فيسبوك»، أعرب عن بالغ التقدير للكونجرس الأمريكى لتكريمه اسم الرئيس الراحل أنور السادات

أبي.. معالم شخصيته

text:
رؤية مصر الحكيمة
رغم كل المعارك والصراعات التى تدور حول مصر وفى منطقة الشرق الأوسط، تظل مصر بؤرة الحكمة، ولها رؤية تقول إن الصراعات والحروب ليست الحل، بل الحوار الناضج بين أطراف الصراعات، وذلك للوصول إلى سلام، من أجل البشر المحصورين فى هذه الصراعات، والذين ينالون القتل والدمار والتشتت والجوع بدون رحمة، وهم لا ناقة لهم ولا جمل فيه.
فتوضح السياسة المصرية رؤية مصر الصائبة والواضحة فى كيفية تجنيب العالم المزيد من المعاناة نتيجة للصراعات والحروب. لقد أوضح الوزير عبدالعاطى سياسة مصر، خلال مشاركته فى الاجتماع الوزارى لمجموعة السبع المنعقد فى باريس، أن تغليب المسارات الدبلوماسية بات ضرورة لا بديل عنها لتجاوز الأزمة مع إيران، للحيلولة دون انزلاق المنطقة إلى مواجهة عسكرية جديدة. وشدد على حتمية إنهاء الوضع المأساوى فى قطاع غزة، وهو ما يعيد تأكيد حقيقة أن قضية فلسطين هى القضية الأم التى تتفرع منها بقية القضايا. إن الحكمة لا تولد بين يوم وليلة، فليت القائمين على علاج مشكلات العلاقات الدولية يدرسون جيدًا رؤية مصر، ويستمعون لصوت الحكمة.

title: الإنجازات لا تمنح حصانة من المساءلة

text:
الإنجازات لا تمنح حصانة من المساءلة
ليس غريباً أن يبدأ النقاش حول أى حادث كبير بالبحث عن أخطاء التشغيل والإدارة والرقابة والصيانة. لكن الغريب فى مصر أن هذه الأسئلة سرعان ما تتراجع أمام تفسير سياسى جاهز، هو تحميل الإخوان المسؤولية. وهذا ما حدث عقب حادث قطار العياط، إذ كشفت تحقيقات النيابة العامة أن السائق عطّل نظام التحكم الآلى، وأن مسؤولين بالمحطة تقاعسوا عن متابعة الإشارات، وأن دفتر الإشارات جرى التلاعب فيه لإخفاء التقصير. وهى وقائع تستدعى المحاسبة، لكنها لم تمنع ظهور رواية المؤامرة. وهكذا يصبح البحث عن خصم من الماضى أكثر إلحاحاً من البحث عن أسباب الإخفاق فى الحاضر. ولا يعنى ذلك تبرئة الماضى، لكن جعله شماعة دائمة يضعف الرواية ويصرف الانتباه عن المسؤوليات الفعلية.
وتبرز قضية وزير النقل كامل الوزير مثالاً على الخلط بين الإنجاز والمحاسبة. فمنذ توليه الوزارة عام 2019 شهد القطاع مشروعات تطوير واستثمارات كبيرة، لكن الحوادث الخطيرة فى السكك الحديدية والطرق لم تتوقف. وليس المطلوب تحميل الوزير خطأ كل سائق أو موظف، لكن من حق المجتمع أن يسأل عن حصيلة الأداء العام، وكفاءة الرقابة والصيانة والسلام
ai_summary: The article argues that infrastructure achievements do not exempt officials from accountability regarding operational failures and safety issues in the transport sector.

Further job losses and programme cuts at the BBC will be more noticeable to audiences than previous savings measures, a new report has warned.
The corporation announced plans earlier this year to cut about 1,800 roles and close some programmes and services, but it has further savings to make to reach its Â£500m target.
In its report, the National Audit Office (NAO) anticipated the BBC's next round of cost-cutting measures will be more difficult to deliver and more perceptible to audiences.
The BBC welcomed the report and said it has "consistently argued that the current funding model is not sustainable and needs reform".
The NAO's report also said the BBC's current measures are expected to reduce the BBC's workforce by 11% over three years.
Gareth Davies, head of the NAO, said: "As the BBC approaches charter renewal in just over a year's time, there is no doubt that there are difficult choices ahead."

title: Iran intensifies Hormuz tanker attacks just as oil prices slide

text:
Iran’s attacks on oil tankers crossing the crucial Strait of Hormuz are getting more intense, just as prices have tumbled due to a flood of supply from the Middle East.
After a period of low-grade clashes, attacks increased in October and continued at the higher tempo this month, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. In a sign of the mounting severity, at least two seafarers are missing after attacks this week. Traders and shipowners also circulated videos of a vessel engulfed in flames this week, though the footage could not be immediately verified.
The flareups are happening as Brent crude futures slid about a fifth this month as Middle East exports approached prewar levels, with the International Energy Agency last week saying that supply is outpacing demand for the first time since the war began. However, flows appear to have pulled back recently, though it’s not clear whether that’s due to intensifying attacks, with shipments often volatile from week to week and month to month.

title: Tokyo Salone wants to make Japan’s creative circles less exclusive
summary: From Pixar to NASA, practitioners shared ideas across disciplines and generations.
text:
What connects a Japanese cookbook designer, a Pixar animation specialist, a coffee equipment maker and a former NASA researcher? At Tokyo American Club in Azabudai on Nov. 14, they were among more than 100 practitioners brought together for the inaugural edition of Tokyo Salone, a gathering designed to encourage creative exchange across disciplines and challenge the insularity of Japan’s creative establishment.
The format was developed over two years by executive curator Ana Arriola-Kanada, who has lived in Japan on and off for 35 years. She sees the country’s creative industries as hampered by gatekeeping, with professional recognition and opportunities too often confined to established networks.
“They like to just keep it within their own communities, their own circle of friends,” she says. “And more often than not, it’s a bit of the patriarchy.”

text:
Seoul subway union launches 'work-to-rule' campaign over hiring, wage dispute
SEOUL, Nov. 20 (Yonhap) -- Unionized workers at Seoul Metro launched a "work-to-rule" campaign Friday as they remain locked in a dispute with management over hiring and wages.
Under the collective action that began at 6 a.m., participants will fully adhere to safety regulations, such as maintaining train speeds regardless of subway schedules, in a move expected to slow down operations.
The union plans to continue the collective action and launch an indefinite strike next Wednesday unless the management responds to its demands for an additional hiring of 1,313 personnel and a wage increase of 3.5 percent.
It has also called for the management to scrap a plan to cut 2,212 jobs.
 Unionized workers of Korea Railroad Corp. (KORAIL) have also warned of launching an indefinite general strike on Dec. 10, demanding the hiring of more safety-related personnel.

Seoul shares open sharply lower tracking U.S. losses after Anthropic debut
SEOUL, Nov. 20 (Yonhap) -- Seoul shares opened sharply lower Friday, tracking overnight losses on Wall Street, as Anthropic's solid market debut failed to ease concerns over whether heavy investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure will generate returns.
The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) fell 209.38 points, or 4.08 percent, to 4,928.51 at the opening bell.
Overnight, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 2.19 percent, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite declined 2.25 percent.
 Investors are awaiting further evidence that heavy investment in the AI sector will generate sustainable returns, despite Anthropic's successful market debut.

text:
Core inflation in Japan soared to a fresh high in 2026, coming in at 2.2% in October as higher energy costs and their knock-on effects pushed up prices in the wider economy.
Core inflation, which strips out prices of food, was lower than the 2.3% expected by Reuters-polled economists, but was higher than the 2.1% in prior month.
Headline inflation came in at 2.3% compared with September's 2.1%, while the so-called "core-core" inflation, which strips out prices of fresh food and energy, dipped slightly to 2.2% from 2.4% in the month before, government data released on Friday showed.
Energy subsidies for households expired in September, exposing consumers to higher prices brought about by the Iran war. Energy prices climbed 2.2% in October, a sharp spike from the 0.6% decline in September. Gas prices jumped 5.8% compared to the 2.4% rise the month before.
Fuel, light and water charges also saw a considerable acceleration, increasing 3.4% compared to last month's 0.8%.

As storms pound both coasts on Wednesday and Thursday, a strong El Niño is once again rearing its head, breaking rainfall records and causing coastal flooding in California and Florida.
Downtown San Francisco set a new record for daily rainfall Wednesday, at 2.64 inches. The previous record was 2.24 inches on Nov. 18, 1918.

The lawsuit, brought by Republican state Sens. Barbara Kirkmeyer of Brighton and Byron Pelton of Sterling, argues that the measure violates the Colorado Taxpayer’s Bill of Rights, also known as TABOR.
Amendment 87, which voters approved in November, replaces the state’s flat 4.4% income tax with a graduated system that charges higher rates based on how much people and businesses earn. To do so, it had to delete a provision of TABOR requiring all income be taxed at the same rate.

“Shipping flows through the Strait of Hormuz have been blocked once, with a hugely disruptive effect on oil and gas markets. It can happen again. Confidence in the Strait as a safe and reliable corridor for energy and other goods has been crushed,” he added.

Instead of rebuilding the waterways with expensive engineering work, conservation teams placed wooden posts and willow branches across selected streams, creating structures that mimicked natural beaver dams. text:
Former Egyptian president Anwar Sadat received a posthumous Congressional Gold Medal, the highest civilian award that the body gives, on Wednesday.
Sadat forged peace with Israel, highlighted by his 1977 visit to Jerusalem, the 1978 Camp David Accords and the 1979 Egypt-Israel peace treaty. Egyptian Islamic Jihad assassinated him in 1981.
Sadat’s vision led to isolation from the Arab world but drew Cairo closer to Washington, and out of the Soviet sphere.
Sadat’s son, Gamal Saat, accepted the award on behalf of his family.

Haiti Regions and Provinces Explained
Haiti’s map has ten departments, but in 2026 the line that matters most to travellers and aid workers is not printed on it: it runs between places armed groups contest and places they do not.
Haiti · Explainer
Haiti is divided into ten departments, the country’s top-level regions, which are split into 42 arrondissements and 149 communes. The word “provinces” is not used in Haiti’s official system, so a search for Haiti provinces leads to the same ten departments.
For readers in the United States, the map matters because the departments are the units in which the UN and aid agencies report displacement and access. The ten regions are not equally exposed, because UN agencies’ 2026 reports place the heaviest pressure from armed groups on Ouest (the West), Artibonite and Centre, a trend we track on our Haiti crisis hub.

Former Liberal MP Sharman Stone has died via voluntary assisted dying after spending much of her political career advocating that people should have autonomy over their bodies.
Dr Stone died aged 75 on Wednesday surrounded by family after a long fight against glioblastoma, an aggressive form of brain cancer.
During her political career, Dr Stone championed contentious medical research and supported access to abortion, and readily - and publicly - disagreed with former leader Tony Abbott on both topics.
Dr Stone was one of the first women superintendents in the Victorian Office of Corrections, the first female director of the Victorian Farmers Federation, and the recipient of an economics PhD.
She was elected to federal parliament in 1996, serving through the Howard years in what was then the seat of Murray in northern Victoria.
Dr Stone was remembered as a strong voice for her local community, right up to her late days.

Meloni, who leads the far-right Brothers of Italy party, rules in a coalition with the populist League and center-right Forza Italia.

The International Court of Justice (ICJ) has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the predominantly Muslim Rohingya minority in 2017.
The landmark judgement in The Hague on Thursday is the first time a state has been held responsible for genocide at the ICJ.
The case filed by Gambia in 2019 has been closely watched by governments, lawyers, rights groups and Rohingya communities for its implications for how states are judged under the 1948 Genocide Convention.
The court said Myanmar has an obligation to compensate the Rohingya for the violations it committed, with the terms to be determined at a later date.

title: Talk about a pinch point! More than 100MILLION red crabs start their annual migration from the forest to the sea
summary: Striking footage shows masses of crustaceans scuttling sideways across roads, over bridges and through forests on Australia's Christmas Island.
text:
Millions of large red crabs have started their annual migration to the sea.
Striking footage shows masses of crustaceans scuttling sideways across roads, over bridges and through forests on Australia's Christmas Island.
The yearly march – which takes place during 'rainy season' – sees more than 100million crabs move to the sea to breed from the remote territory on the Indian Ocean.
It is hoped the crabs will spawn 'before dawn on a receding high tide during the moon's last quarter' as the timing is tied to lunar cycles, Parks Australia said.
The migration requires 'months of preparation' by conservationists on the island, which lies 350km (217 miles) south of Indonesia and more than a thousand kilometres from the Australian mainland.
'People travel from around the world to witness this incredible wildlife spectacle on Christmas Island,' Parks Australia's Christmas Island National Park Manager Chris Chartres said.

An Asian Development Bank analysis of four decades of weather patterns raises an alarm about the accelerating pace of receding glaciers in Central Asia and the Caucasus.
The ADB assessment, titled Glaciers to Farms Climate Risk and Capacity Assessment, evaluated glaciers and water-usage patterns associated with three river basins – the Naryn and Pyanj in Central Asia, and the Kura in the Caucasus. The report noted that Caucasus glaciers are receding at the fastest pace. Average temperatures could be up to 5°C higher across both regions by 2085 than at present, it adds.

How IMF loans created Egypt’s decade of economic decay
Egypt has signed a string of loan agreements with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) over the past ten years, the latest of which expires this December. The Fund maintains that the “reforms” it prescribed have made the economy more resilient to shocks. The crises of recent months, regional and global, say otherwise: the economy has become more fragile, not less.
In ten years, external debt has roughly tripled, the economy has leaned more heavily on foreign borrowing to finance it, and the pound has lost about 84% of its value. Millions of Egyptians have watched their living standards collapse under successive waves of price rises, all under austerity programs the government agreed to with the IMF.

Zohran Mamdani, New York City’s mayor, has signed a bill that will bring the city’s horse-drawn carriage industry to an end by 1 June 2028.
Known as Romanch’s Law, the legislation is named after 18-year-old Indian tourist, Romanch Mahajan, who was killed in June after being thrown from a carriage in Central Park when a horse became startled. The law marks the end of an industry that has operated in the city for more than a century.
The legislation has been divisive, with workers’ unions opposing the ban over concerns about lost livelihoods, while animal rights activists have backed the move, citing longstanding concerns over horse welfare, including cases in which horses have died from exhaustion.
During Thursday’s signing, Mamdani said: “For 150 years, horse-drawn carriages have been a fixture of Central Park. Today, we are bringing that chapter to a close. This industry will come to an end, and we have a responsibility to the workers whose livelihoods depend on it. We will work along
ai_summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani signed legislation banning horse-drawn carriages by 2028 following safety and animal welfare concerns.

This should come as no great surprise: young people are more keenly aware of the significance of social class than those who came before them. The yawning gap in life chances at birth is something they know better than complacent older generations. Class may be unfashionable in the language of politics – long damned by the right as the politics of envy, avoided by many on the left for fear of sounding chip-on-the-shoulder – yet it’s part of the daily experience for young people.

text:
All eyes this week are on Shenzhen, where leaders of the APEC grouping will meet for their annual summit. The summit, however, is being overshadowed by the first-ever sit-down between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. As significant as this is, it is arguably not the most important political development in China this week. On Monday, the Communist Party published a revised set of regulations detailing how the country will be governed in the years ahead.
The Regulations on the Work of Local Committees of the Communist Party of China govern every local Party committee and its standing committee at the provincial, city and county levels. These committees, and not the governments they oversee, are the real seat of power in China. They set the direction, decide major issues, manage cadres and supervise the legislatures, governments, courts and procuratorates in their jurisdictions. The rules that bind them are, in effect, the operating manual for governing China below Beijing.

title: Pakistan military says it killed 22 militants in raids on hideouts
summary: Pakistan’s military says security forces have raided militant hideouts in the northwest near the Afghan border, setting off gunbattles that killed 22 militants
text:
Pakistani security forces acting on intelligence raided militant hideouts in the northwest near the Afghan border, setting off gunbattles that killed 22 militants, the military said Thursday (November 19, 2026).
It alleged that the militants killed were backed by neighboring India. There was no immediate comment from New Delhi, but Pakistan often accuses Afghanistan and India of supporting the Pakistani Taliban and other militant groups, allegations both countries deny.
The raids took place over the past 48 hours in the South Waziristan, Bannu and Tank districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, the military said in a statement.
The military reported last week that security forces had killed 74 militants over several days in raids on hideouts in the northwest and in southwestern Balochistan province.
The military said troops were searching the areas for any remaining militants and pledged to continue operations against what it described as foreign-backed terrorism.

title: Ukraine's NATO membership is relevant for European security, Macron says
summary: BERLIN, Nov 19 - French President Emmanuel Macron said the question of NATO membership for Ukraine was \"relevant\" for European security, given the country's strong and well equipped army.
text:
Ukraine's NATO membership is relevant for European security, Macron says
BERLIN, Nov 19 - French President Emmanuel Macron said the question of NATO membership for Ukraine was "relevant" for European security, given the country's strong and well equipped army.
"I think we must reopen the question of Ukraine's membership to NATO," Macron told reporters after a Berlin summit of leaders of European countries supporting Ukraine, called the "Coalition of the Willing", along with the presence of U.S. President Donald Trump's special envoys for Ukraine.
The European leaders present in Berlin had an exchange with Trump, Macron added.
"We had the opportunity to have the two special envoys, Mr. Kushner and Mr. Witkoff, of President Trump, who was able to have an exchange with us during this summit," Macron told reporters. REUTERS

title: Timetable set out for dismantling leasehold system in England and Wales
summary: Under the government's plans, a ban on the sale of most new leasehold flats is expected around 2031.
text:
Timetable set out for dismantling leasehold system in England and Wales
- Published
The government has set out a timetable for when the leasehold system in England and Wales will be dismantled.
Under the plans, most new flats - with only limited exemptions - will be sold as commonhold, where residents collectively own and manage their buildings.
The government says a modernised commonhold model is expected to be up and running around 2029, followed by a ban on the sale of most new leasehold flats, expected around 2031.
Meanwhile, a Â£250 cap on ground rents - the annual fee paid by leaseholders to their freeholder - is expected to come into force in 2028, six months after a new law passes.
Ground rents will then be reduced to a "peppercorn" rate - which is effectively nothing - after 40 years.
There are around five million leasehold homes in England and Wales, where people own the right to occupy a property via a lease for a limited number of years from a freeholder.

نال الفنان إبراهيم حسين تقدير الامتياز في مشروع تخرجه بكلية الفنون الجميلة عام 1967، بعدما اختار قصة النبي نوح موضوعًا للوحتين كبيرتين، صوّر فيهما أفراد العائلة عند خروجها من الفلك، بحسب شهادة زميله الفنان إلهامي نجيب.
وقال نجيب في تصريحات خاصة لـ«المصري اليوم»، إنه تعرّف على إبراهيم في السنة الإعدادية بالكلية، وسرعان ما نشأت بينهما صداقة بسبب اهتماماتهما المشتركة وتقاربهما في السكن، مشيرًا إلى أن نبوغه في الرسم ظهر مبكرًا قبل التحاقه بقسم الحفر «الجرافيك».
ووصف صديقه بأنه طالب دؤوب لا يمل التجريب، أتقن الرسم والحفر على الزنك والخشب واللينوليوم، ثم اتجه إلى تجربة الفلوماستر الكحولي سريع الجفاف، الذي يتطلب دقة لعدم إتاحته تصحيح الأخطاء بسهولة.

text:
A new report from the state's power grid warns that Long Island could face an electricity shortage for the first time in its history.
The New York Independent System Operator projects electricity demand to outpace supply by 2030, unless an unpopular new project that many Long Islanders have vocally opposed moves forward.
The Propel NY Energy Project, which has not begun construction, plans to lay 90 miles of underground transmission lines connecting Long Island to the rest of the state.
However, the project, spearheaded by the New York Power Authority and New York Transco, has drawn fierce opposition over concerns like traffic and the environment.
Work is anticipated to begin this spring.

Nov 19 - Russia's Prosecutor General's Office said on Thursday that the Wikimedia Foundation, which oversees Wikipedia and other information projects, could be branded undesirable under Russian law on grounds of destabilising the country.
A statement by the office, quoted by Interfax news agency, said it had issued a warning about the possibility of declaring Wikimedia undesirable.
"The Prosecutor General's Office...has established facts that Wikimedia Foundation, Inc. is conducting a targeted information campaign to destabilise the situation on the territory of the Russian Federation," the statement said.
It said it had warned of punitive measures to be applied "in the instance that the destructive anti-Russian activity continues".
The Wikimedia Foundation did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Russia regularly brands entities it says undermine its constitutional order or national security as "undesirable"

text:
Rohingya genocide: What was said in court and what happens now?
Myanmar has been found guilty of committing genocide against its Rohingya minority by the International Court of Justice (ICJ).
The verdict marks the first time a state has ever been found to have committed genocide by an international court.
The court found on Thursday that "genocidal intent is the only reasonable inference that can be drawn from the evidence" it had seen.
The verdict was reached by a majority of nine votes to six among a panel of judges from around the world.
The BBC's Anna Holligan is in the Hague and reports on what the ICJ's ruling means.

title: Third Ukrainian strike in 4 days halts rail traffic on Russia's Kerch Bridge to Crimea
summary: The attack came hours before the start of talks in Berlin between U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy alongside more than 40 European leaders who are supporting Ukraine's war effort
text:
A third Ukrainian aerial attack in four days on the key Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Russian-held Crimea halted rail traffic across the span, officials said Thursday (November 19, 2026), after earlier strikes shut down the road section of the landmark that is a symbol of Moscow's invasion.
Train traffic across the bridge stopped after the overnight strike while authorities assessed the damage, but it resumed in the afternoon, according to Russian state news agency RIA Novosti.
The Ukrainian strikes seemed calculated to embarrass Russian President Vladimir Putin as he met in China with President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump, as well as to demonstrate that Kyiv still holds cards in the war and to undermine Russia's argument that its victory is inevitable.
The attack came hours before the start of talks in Berlin between U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy alongside more than 40 European leaders who are supporting Ukraine
ai_summary: Ukrainian forces conducted a third aerial strike in four days on the Kerch Bridge, temporarily halting rail traffic between Russia and Crimea.

title: Egypt and France in joint naval exercise
summary: Egypt and France in joint naval exercise APAnews - Agence de Presse Africaine
text:
The Egyptian and French navies, on Wednesday launched a joint military exercise in the Mediterranean, focused on operational coordination, countering maritime threats, and drone detection.
The joint exercise named Cleopatra-2026 began in the Mediterranean, within the operational area of Egypt’s Northern Fleet, and will continue for several days, said the spokesperson for the Egyptian Armed Forces.
This exercise involves several naval units from both countries. The first phase was devoted to a series of theoretical and practical sessions aimed at harmonising cooperation procedures and strengthening interoperability among the participating forces.
The training focuses in particular on the planning and conduct of joint maritime operations, as well as on countering various maritime threats and drones. These activities aim to develop the operational capabilities of both navies, improve their coordination, and promote the sharing of expertise in the fields of maritime security.

Sexual assaults in Ceuta have increased by 650 per cent since 80,000 migrants from Morocco flooded the enclave in late July, according to a report.
Documents on emergency service calls obtained by Spanish outlet El Español revealed that sexual assaults rose sharply from four to 30 between July 30 and October 29 in 2025 and the same period in 2026.
Sixteen of those cases involved minors, compared with none during the same period the previous year.
The figures also show a dramatic rise in violent attacks involving weapons, with cases classified as 'firearm assaults' jumping from eight to 56 and reports of 'assaults with bladed weapons' surging from 23 to 268.

Joanne Young, who has waived her right to anonymity, spoke outside of Winchester Court and encouraged people to speak out against violence against women and girls.
Four men have been found guilty of sexually abusing Young in the first trial of its kind in the UK.
Philip Young, 50, already pleaded guilty to multiple charges of drugging and raping his wife over a 13-year period at their home in Swindon, Wiltshire.
Norman Macksoni, 48, Richard Wilkins, 62, Connor Sanderson-Doyle, 32, and Mohammed Hassan, 38, were found guilty of multiple sexual offences by a jury at Winchester Crown Court. Wilkins and Macksoni were each found guilty of one count of rape.

title: Are ‘natural’, ‘herbal’ toothpastes healthier alternatives?
summary: Whatever else a toothpaste contains, an appropriate amount of fluoride currently remains one of the simplest and cost-effective ways to protect teeth.
text:
Natural, herbal and organic toothpastes are becoming familiar sights on shop shelves, often promoted as healthier alternatives to conventional products. Some contain ingredients such as aloe vera, neem or green tea. But before changing toothpaste, there is one important question to consider: does it contain fluoride?
Fluoride is a mineral that helps protect teeth against decay. Some toothpastes marketed as natural contain it, while others do not. The words on the front of the tube cannot tell us whether a product will protect our teeth.
These terms are often used interchangeably, although they mean different things. “Natural” usually describes ingredients derived from natural sources. “Herbal” refers to plant-based ingredients, while “organic” generally describes ingredients produced to particular farming standards. None of these labels, on its own, shows that a toothpaste can prevent tooth decay.

ai_summary: Consumers are advised to check for fluoride content in natural or herbal toothpastes, as marketing labels do not guarantee protection against tooth decay.

summary: Hundreds of ancient coffins found in a Ptolemaic cemetery at Tell Abu Billou, Egypt Archaeology News Online Magazine
text:
Egyptian archaeologists at Tell Abu Billou in Menoufia Governorate have uncovered a large burial ground. The Supreme Council of Antiquities says the graves date from the end of the Late Period through the Ptolemaic era and into early Roman rule.
The team found an open courtyard filled with burials. Hundreds of stone and clay coffins lie in the top layer, along with traces of wooden ones. Builders also made several vaulted tombs from mud brick and one tomb lined inside with limestone. Walls still run under the sand and rubble in several directions, so the full layout isn’t clear yet. title: No mention of fossil fuels in latest COP31 draft deal
summary: One of the most fraught debates at the UN climate talks in Turkey has revolved around the future of coal, oil and gas. Now, all mention of fossil fuels has been removed from the summit's new draft agreement.
text:
Fossil fuels dropped from latest COP31 draft deal
Published November 19, 2026last updated November 19, 2026
Climate negotiators have removed any mention of fossil fuels — the main source of greenhouse gas emissions heating the planet — in a new draft deal published by COP31 summit co-host Australia.
The latest text released Thursday at the UN climate conference in Turkey stripped out two references to a transition away from coal, oil and gas and a call for an accelerated phaseout that had been in an earlier draft.
This slimmed down version follows days of tough negotiations, with representatives from nearly 200 nations debating issues such as the future of fossil fuels and climate funding for developing countries.
The text still includes a call to increase the global share of final energy demand met by electricity to 35% by 2035 — up from around 20% today — a proposal that was pushed by host Turkey.
It did not specify whether that additional electricity needs to come from clean sources
ai_summary: Negotiators at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey removed references to phasing out fossil fuels from the latest draft of the international agreement.

OVERVIEW
El Niño conditions are underway and are forecasted to strengthen through late 2026, coinciding with a strong positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD).
Key Messages
I. A high-confidence dry season is forecasted for central and southern parts of Southern Africa. Seasonal forecasts indicate an increased likelihood of below-normal rainfall, prolonged dry spells and above-normal temperatures, while above-normal rainfall and flooding risks are expected in parts of the northern areas of the region.
II. The region remains highly vulnerable following the severe 2023/24 El Niño, which affected an estimated 54.4 million people and contributed to widespread food insecurity, livelihood losses and disease outbreaks. Currently, humanitarian needs remain elevated, with 11 million acutely food insecure people across the region, while funding levels remain low.
III. Southern Africa experienced one of its largest cholera outbreaks during 2024-25, increasing public health concerns entering the 2026/27
ai_summary: El Niño conditions and a positive Indian Ocean Dipole are forecasted to cause severe drought and food insecurity across Southern Africa through late 2026.

title: Suspended bishop withdraws suit against Anglican Primate, gives reason
summary: The latest development occurred weeks after the Commissioner of Police in Anambra State, Nnanna Ama, held a peace meeting with the embattled bishops in the state over the crisis. The post Suspended bishop withdraws suit against Anglican Primate, gives reason appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria .
text:
The suspended Bishop of Awka Diocese in Anambra State, Alexander Ibezim, has withdrawn his lawsuit challenging his suspension by the Primate of the Church of Nigeria (Anglican Communion), Henry Ndukuba.
The suspension and lawsuit
PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the primate had suspended the archbishop for six months over various allegations, including selling church land for N2 billion.
The suspension, according to the primate, was to allow for transparent investigations into allegations against the archbishop and the diocese.
Mr Ndukuba also announced the appointment of the Bishop of the Diocese of Aguata, Samuel Ezeofor,
as the supervising bishop of the church’s Diocese of Awka and coordinating bishop of the Province of the Niger.
This newspaper also reported that Mr Ibezim subsequently filed a lawsuit in which he challenged his suspension and plan to discipline him.
Withdrawal
Mr Ibezim had filed the suit at the High Court of Anambra State, Awka Judicial Division on 13 October.

Bahrain cracks down on Shiite clerics as Iran attacks

You're reading an excerpt from Al-Monitor Washington, where we break down the latest in US-Middle East diplomacy. To read the full newsletter, sign up here.
WASHINGTON — Bahrain has imprisoned dozens of Shiite clerics while under Iranian attack, the latest in a crackdown that risks drawing the small Gulf country further into the confrontation between Tehran and Washington.
Days after Iran resumed airstrikes on US targets in Bahrain, a Bahraini criminal court on Monday sentenced 64 defendants to life in prison and five others to 15-year terms over alleged collaboration with the Iranian government. Nairobi — Scholars and legal practitioners from several countries have called for stronger international cooperation on artificial intelligence (AI) and data governance, warning that the rapid growth of digital technologies risks deepening inequalities if countries and communities are excluded from shaping the rules.
The experts said fair digital governance must go beyond technological development to address data privacy, national sovereignty, accountability and equitable access to the benefits of the digital economy.
The concerns featured prominently at the inaugural Global Forum on Digital Intelligence, Rule of Law and Interdisciplinary Governance, hosted by the University of Nairobi's Faculty of Law on November 17, bringing together participants from Kenya, China, South Africa, Japan, the United States and other countries.
